sentences.text: Rajesh vs State Of M.P on 5 March, 2025
Author: Rajesh Bindal

Bench: Rajesh Bindal
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2025
 (@ Slp(Crl.) No. 16970/2024)
 Rajesh Appellant(S)
 Versus
 State Of M.P. Respondent(S)
 O R D E R
1. Leave granted.

2. The appellant had been convicted by the Trial Court for the offences punishable under Sections 304B, 306 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.
Accordingly, a sentence of ten years of rigorous imprisonment and fine had been imposed on the appellant.
Pending his appeal against the aforesaid conviction and sentence, the appellants application for suspension of sentence has been rejected by the High Court, vide the impugned order.
3. Admittedly, the appellant has undergone almost half of the sentence that has been imposed on him.
4. In such view of the matter, we are inclined to set aside the impugned order and suspend the sentence of the appellant, till the disposal of the criminal appeal by the High Court.

5. Accordingly, the impugned order stands set aside and the appellants sentence stands suspended,
subject to the terms and conditions that may be imposed by the Trial Court, as deemed fit for the aforesaid purpose.
6. The appeal is allowed, accordingly.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
J. [M.M. SUNDRESH] J.
[RAJESH BINDAL] NEW DELHI;
